translation_direction: fr → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete French electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Voltaire’s brisk, deadpan irony and the dialogue run on inside paragraphs are kept, with the title page and its line breaks reproduced.
decisions.rationale: The satire depends on deadpan pace and unmarked speech.

decisions.decision: Orders, sects and offices are given their Vietnamese ecclesiastical names (dòng Phanxicô, phái Tái Tẩy, á phó tế); the untranslated Italian of the old woman’s refrain is kept.
decisions.rationale: Doctrinal and institutional jokes must stay legible.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: ‘Tái Thẩm’ (a retrial sect) corrected to the Anabaptists’ established name ‘Tái Tẩy’ throughout and in the glossary.
mal physique and mal moral fixed as a stable pair; Andalucía, lieue/mille, ‘tiểu thư Cunégonde’ and ‘Kitô giáo’ made consistent.
‘parricide’ rendered ‘tội giết vua’ and the second-cousin term made precise; subdeacon term unified as ‘á phó tế’.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.rationale: Established Vietnamese name of the Anabaptists; glossed once at first use.

glossary.draft_rendering: cái ác luân lý / cái ác thể chất
glossary.rationale: Martin’s and Pangloss’s paired terms, kept constant through the book.

glossary.draft_rendering: tiểu thư Cunégonde (nàng in tender narration)
glossary.rationale: Courtly register for a baron’s daughter; ‘cô’ avoided.
Distinguishes the French league from the mile.

witness_decision: Selected Project Gutenberg #4650, a transcription of Œuvres de Voltaire, ed. A. J. Q. Beuchot, vol. XXXIII, Romans I (Paris: Lefèvre / Werdet et Lequien fils, 1829). Beuchot’s preface and the volume’s footnotes, whether editorial or authorial, are excluded so that only the narrative text is canonical. First published 1759; not collated with the 1759 editions.

unresolved_questions.explanation: The old woman’s Italian refrain is left untranslated, as in the source; a reader note would help.
Classical and historical names mix international and French forms; a single policy could follow in a patch.

title_review.rationale: Candide, hay Thuyết lạc quan keeps Voltaire’s subtitle in the established Vietnamese form; the formula ‘cái tốt nhất trong mọi thế giới có thể có’ recurs unchanged.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: The fictional title page with its line breaks.
The final line, ‘il faut cultiver notre jardin’.
